name: Lee Kuan Yew
tagline: The founding prime minister who led Singapore from 1959 to 1990.

scenes.title: Born in Singapore
scenes.caption: Lee Kuan Yew is born on 16 September 1923. He studies at Raffles Institution, then at Raffles College on a scholarship.
scenes.visual: A 1920s Singapore street of two-storey shophouses with shuttered windows and five-foot ways. A rickshaw puller and a small schoolboy in white uniform, both seen from behind, walk toward a colonial school building with a clock tower.

scenes.title: The Japanese Occupation
scenes.caption: The Japanese Occupation (1942-1945) interrupts his studies at Raffles College and shapes his view of how fragile Singapore is.
scenes.visual: A blacked-out Singapore street at night during the Japanese occupation. A queue of civilians seen from behind hold ration tins; bicycles lean on a wall; searchlight beams cross a smoky sky.

scenes.title: Law at Cambridge
scenes.caption: After the war he goes to England, transferring to Cambridge in 1947. He graduates in law with a starred first in 1949 and is called to the bar in 1950.
scenes.visual: An English university courtyard with Gothic stone arches and an autumn lawn. A young man in a black academic gown, seen from behind, carries a stack of law books across the grass.

scenes.title: A party, then power
scenes.caption: Political meetings at his home lead to the founding of the People's Action Party in 1954. On 5 June 1959 he is sworn in as prime minister.
scenes.visual: A 1950s living room at night: men seen from behind sit around a round table covered with papers under a hanging lamp and a ceiling fan. Through the open window, a rally crowd and loudspeakers on poles.

scenes.title: Merger and separation
scenes.caption: Singapore joins Malaysia on 16 September 1963. Less than two years later, on 9 August 1965, separation is announced and a visibly emotional Lee breaks down at the press conference.
scenes.visual: A 1965 press conference: a long table crowded with radio microphones and a television camera on a tripod. One speaker sits at the table, seen from behind, facing reporters. A plain wall behind, lit by camera lights.

scenes.title: Building a garden city
scenes.caption: The Housing Board starts in 1960 to clear the housing shortage. In May 1967 Lee sets out a vision of a 'garden city', after the 1963 tree-planting drive.
scenes.visual: New public-housing slab blocks rising behind bamboo scaffolding and a tower crane. In the foreground a man seen from behind plants a young rain tree beside a new road, next to a row of staked saplings.

scenes.title: Stepping down, and farewell
scenes.caption: Lee hands the premiership to Goh Chok Tong on 28 November 1990. He dies on 23 March 2015, aged 91; a week of national mourning follows.
scenes.visual: Night: a long queue of mourners seen from behind, holding umbrellas, winds along a street toward a lit civic building. White chrysanthemums lie along a railing in the foreground.
